records.gloss: And these [were] the ones coming to David to Ziklag while still restrained from [the] face of Saul son of Kish; and they [were] among the mighty men, helpers of the war.
pieces: These are the men who came to David at Ziklag while he still could not move about freely because of Saul son of Kish. They were among the warriors who helped him in battle.

L.1: And these [are] the ones who came to David at Ziklag while he was still restrained from the presence of Saul son of Kish; and they [were] among the mighty men, helpers in the war.

R.1: Some men came to join David at Ziklag. This was while David was still kept away from his own land because of Saul son of Kish. These men were among the brave fighters who helped David in battle.

decisions.choice: Ziklag: the Philistine town where David lived while he fled from Saul
decisions.reason: Achish king of Gath gave David the town of Ziklag when David took refuge among the Philistines to escape Saul (1 Samuel 27:1-7). He lived there a year and four months, until Saul's death (1 Samuel 27:7; 2 Samuel 1:1). Chronicles has just told of Saul's death and of David becoming king (chapters 10-11); here it looks back to show who joined David before that.

decisions.choice: still restrained because of Saul: shut out of his own country and unable to move freely while Saul lived
decisions.reason: The word means held back, shut in or kept away. David was not a prisoner, but Saul's hunt for him kept him out of Israel and in Philistine territory (1 Samuel 27:1, 4).

decisions.choice: among the mighty men, helpers in the war: part of the band of fighters who helped David
decisions.reason: "Mighty men" is the word used for David's famous warriors in 11:10-47. These men belonged to that group of fighters and helped him in his battles. The verb "help" runs through the chapter (verses 18, 19, 20, 22, 23).

decisions.choice: kept away from his own land
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what being held back because of Saul meant for David: he could not live freely in Israel.

records.gloss: Equipped of bow, using right hand and using left hand with stones and with arrows with [the] bow; of [the] kinsmen of Saul, from Benjamin.
pieces: They were armed with bows, and they could sling stones and shoot arrows with either the right hand or the left. They were kinsmen of Saul from Benjamin.

L.2: armed with [the] bow, using the right hand and the left with stones and with arrows from the bow; of the kinsmen of Saul from Benjamin.

R.2: They were archers, and they could use either hand to sling stones or shoot arrows. They came from the tribe of Benjamin and were Saul's own relatives.

decisions.choice: using the right hand and the left: able to use either hand
decisions.reason: These fighters could shoot and sling equally well with either hand. Benjamin was known for skilled left-handed fighters (Judges 3:15; 20:16), and the name Benjamin means "son of the right hand".

decisions.choice: with stones: slung stones
decisions.reason: Stones were hurled with a sling, the weapon of Benjamin's left-handed men in Judges 20:16 and of David himself (1 Samuel 17:40, 49).

decisions.choice: kinsmen of Saul from Benjamin: men of Saul's own tribe
decisions.reason: The first men named as joining David came from Saul's own tribe. Chronicles shows that even Saul's kinsmen saw where the kingdom was going (compare verse 30).

decisions.choice: sling stones
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the action, slinging, which the Hebrew leaves to be understood.

pieces: Their chief was Ahiezer, and next came Joash, both sons of Shemaah the Gibeathite. There were also Jeziel and Pelet the sons of Azmaveth, and Beracah and Jehu the Anathothite.

L.3: The chief [was] Ahiezer, and Joash, sons of Shemaah the Gibeathite; and Jeziel and Pelet, sons of Azmaveth; and Beracah and Jehu the Anathothite,

R.3: Ahiezer was their leader, and next was Joash. They were sons of Shemaah from Gibeah. Jeziel and Pelet, the sons of Azmaveth, were there too, and so were Beracah and Jehu from Anathoth.

decisions.choice: the Gibeathite, the Anathothite: from Gibeah and from Anathoth
decisions.reason: These names say where a man came from. Gibeah was Saul's own town (1 Samuel 10:26), and Anathoth was a town of Benjamin given to the priests (Joshua 21:18).

decisions.choice: Jeziel: the name as it is read aloud
alternatives: Jeziel (written with a different vowel letter)
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew text spells this name slightly differently; the traditional reading, followed here, gives Jeziel. The man is the same either way.

decisions.choice: complete sentences for each group
decisions.reason: The Hebrew list of names runs on from verse 3 to verse 8. Literal keeps it as one list; Balanced and Readable give each verse its own sentence. Readable uses the place names ("from Gibeah").

records.gloss: and Ishmaiah the Gibeonite, a mighty [man] among the Thirty and over the Thirty,
pieces: Ishmaiah the Gibeonite was a mighty warrior among the Thirty and a leader over the Thirty.

L.4: and Ishmaiah the Gibeonite, a mighty man among the Thirty and over the Thirty;

R.4: Ishmaiah from Gibeon was there too. He was one of David's famous warriors called the Thirty, and he was a leader over them.

decisions.choice: verse numbers: the Hebrew text divides this verse in two
decisions.reason: This translation numbers verses as the Hebrew text does. Here the Hebrew ends verse 4 after "over the Thirty" and makes the next names (Jeremiah to Jozabad the Gederathite) verse 5. Many Bibles join the two into one verse 4, so from verse 5 to the end of the chapter their numbers are one lower than here (Hebrew 12:5-41 is 12:4-40 in those Bibles). The words are the same; only the numbers differ.

decisions.choice: the Thirty: David's company of famous warriors
decisions.reason: The Thirty were David's best-known fighting men, listed in 11:11-47 and 2 Samuel 23:8-39. Ishmaiah is not named in those lists; here he is both one of them and a leader over them.

decisions.choice: the Gibeonite: from Gibeon
decisions.reason: Gibeon was a town in the land of Benjamin (Joshua 18:25), so Ishmaiah belongs with the Benjaminites of verse 2.

decisions.choice: the Korahites: men of a family called after Korah
decisions.reason: Korahites are usually the Levite family descended from Korah (Exodus 6:24; 1 Chronicles 9:19). Since this list is of Benjaminites (verse 2), these may instead be a Benjaminite family named after another Korah. The text does not say which.

R.8: And Joelah and Zebadiah, the sons of Jeroham from Gedor, joined David too.

decisions.choice: Gedor: a town, not certainly identified
decisions.reason: A Gedor in the hill country of Judah is named in Joshua 15:58, and a Benjaminite family named Gedor appears in 8:31 and 9:37. Which is meant here is not known.

records.gloss: And from the Gadites separated themselves to David to [the] stronghold toward [the] wilderness, mighty men of the valor, men of [the] army for the war, arranging shield and spear; and faces of a lion [were] their faces, and like gazelles on the mountains to hasten.
pieces: Some Gadites broke away and went over to David at the stronghold in the wilderness. They were mighty warriors, trained soldiers ready for battle, skilled with shield and spear. Their faces were the faces of lions, and on the mountains they ran as swiftly as gazelles.

L.9: And from the Gadites [some] separated themselves to David at the stronghold in the wilderness, mighty men of valor, men of the army for war, handling shield and spear; and their faces [were] the faces of a lion, and [they were] like gazelles on the mountains for swiftness.

R.9: Some men from the tribe of Gad left their people and joined David at his fortress in the desert. They were brave warriors, trained for war and skilled with shields and spears. They looked as fierce as lions, and they could run as fast as gazelles on the mountains.

decisions.choice: the stronghold in the wilderness: David's refuge while Saul hunted him
decisions.reason: Before David went to Ziklag he hid in strongholds in the wilderness of Judah (1 Samuel 22:4-5; 23:14). The Gadites came to him there, so the chapter is not in time order: it gathers all who joined David before he became king.

decisions.choice: separated themselves: broke with their own tribe to join David
decisions.reason: The verb means to separate or set oneself apart. Gad lived east of the Jordan, and these men left Saul's side to go over to David.

decisions.choice: faces of a lion ... like gazelles on the mountains: fierce and fast
decisions.reason: Two pictures praise the Gadites: they looked as fierce as lions, and they were as quick on their feet as gazelles in the hills. David's lament praises Saul and Jonathan with the same kinds of picture (2 Samuel 1:23), and Asahel is called as swift as a gazelle (2 Samuel 2:18).

decisions.choice: mighty men of valor: strong, brave warriors
decisions.reason: The phrase names seasoned fighting men (Joshua 1:14; 10:7; 2 Kings 24:14). It recurs in verses 22, 26, 29 and 31 and is given the same wording each time.

decisions.choice: mighty warriors (B); brave warriors (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "mighty men of valor". Balanced says "mighty warriors", as in 2 Kings 5:1 and 24:14, and Readable "brave warriors"; the same words are used for this phrase throughout the chapter.

decisions.reason: The eleven Gadites are listed by rank, from the chief down to the eleventh (verses 10-14).

decisions.choice: one and ten: eleventh
decisions.reason: Hebrew forms the number eleven as "one ten"; here it gives Machbannai's rank.

records.source: אֵ֥לֶּה מִבְּנֵי־גָ֖ד רָאשֵׁ֣י הַצָּבָ֑א אֶחָ֤ד לְמֵאָה֙ הַקָּטָ֔ן וְהַגָּד֖וֹל לְאָֽלֶף׃
records.gloss: These from [the] sons of Gad [were] heads of the army; one to a hundred the least, and the greatest to a thousand.
pieces: These Gadites were army officers. The least of them could stand against a hundred, and the greatest against a thousand.

L.15: These from the sons of Gad [were] heads of the army; the least [was] one for a hundred, and the greatest for a thousand.

R.15: These men from Gad were army officers. The weakest of them could take on a hundred men, and the strongest could take on a thousand.

decisions.choice: the least for a hundred, the greatest for a thousand: even the weakest was equal to a hundred men
alternatives: the least was over a hundred, and the greatest over a thousand
decisions.reason: The words can be read as praise of their strength, like "five of you will chase a hundred" (Leviticus 26:8) and "how could one chase a thousand" (Deuteronomy 32:30). They can also be read as their rank: the least of them commanded a hundred men and the greatest a thousand. The praise fits the lions and gazelles of verse 9; the rank fits "heads of the army" just before.

decisions.choice: heads of the army: officers
decisions.reason: "Heads" here are leaders in the army. Verse 19 says David made some of these newcomers leaders of his band.

decisions.choice: the weakest ... the strongest
decisions.reason: "The least" and "the greatest" here compare the men's strength, which Readable says in plain words.

records.gloss: These [were] they who crossed the Jordan in the month the first, and it [was] overflowing over all its banks, and they put to flight all the valleys, to the east and to the west.
pieces: These men crossed the Jordan in the first month, while the river was flooding over all its banks, and they put to flight everyone in the valleys, east and west.

L.16: These [were] the ones who crossed the Jordan in the first month, when it was overflowing all its banks, and they put to flight all the valleys, to the east and to the west.

R.16: These men crossed the Jordan River in the first month of the year, in early spring, when it was flooding over all its banks. They chased away all the people living in the valleys on both sides of the river.

decisions.choice: in the first month, when it overflowed its banks: the Jordan in spring flood
decisions.reason: The first month of the year fell in spring, when the snow on the northern mountains melts and the Jordan runs high (Joshua 3:15; 4:19). Crossing it then was dangerous, and the Gadites did it to reach David.

decisions.choice: put to flight all the valleys: drove away the people of the valleys
decisions.reason: "The valleys" stands for the people who lived in them. Who these were, and whether they were enemies on the way to David, the text does not say.

decisions.choice: everyone in the valleys (B); all the people living in the valleys (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say outright that it was the people of the valleys who fled.

decisions.choice: the first month of the year, in early spring
decisions.reason: Readable adds the season so the reader sees why the river was in flood.

records.gloss: And came some of [the] sons of Benjamin and Judah to the stronghold to David.
pieces: Some men of Benjamin and Judah also came to David at the stronghold.

L.17: And some of the sons of Benjamin and Judah came to the stronghold, to David.

R.17: Some men from the tribes of Benjamin and Judah also came to David at his fortress.

decisions.choice: the stronghold: as in verse 9
decisions.reason: This is David's refuge in the wilderness of Judah while Saul hunted him (1 Samuel 22:4-5; 23:14), not Ziklag.

decisions.choice: men of Benjamin and Judah
decisions.reason: "Sons of" here means members of the tribe. These were fighting men, so Balanced and Readable say "men".

records.gloss: And went out David before them and answered and said to them, If for peace you have come to me to help me, will be to me toward you a heart for together; and if to betray me to my adversaries, with no violence in my palms, may see [the] God of our fathers and rebuke.
pieces: David went out to meet them and said to them, "If you have come to me in peace to help me, then my heart is one with yours. But if you are here to betray me to my enemies, though I have done no wrong, may the God of our ancestors see it and rebuke you."

L.18: And David went out before them and answered and said to them, "If you have come to me in peace to help me, my heart will be one with you; but if [you have come] to betray me to my adversaries, though [there is] no violence in my hands, may the God of our fathers see and rebuke [it]."

R.18: David went out to meet them. He said to them, "If you have come as friends to help me, I will gladly join with you. But if you have come to hand me over to my enemies, even though I have done nothing wrong, may the God of our ancestors see it and punish you."

decisions.choice: my heart will be one with you: I will be fully united with you
decisions.reason: The words say David will be wholly bound to them in loyalty and purpose if they come as friends. The "one heart" of all Israel in verse 39 echoes it.

decisions.choice: no violence in my hands: I have done no wrong
decisions.reason: Hands stand for what a person does. David claims he has done nothing to deserve being handed over (compare Job 16:17).

decisions.choice: may the God of our fathers see and rebuke: let God judge between us
decisions.reason: David leaves the matter to God, as Jacob did with Laban: "God saw my affliction ... and rebuked you" (Genesis 31:42). The verb means to decide a case and to rebuke the one in the wrong.

decisions.choice: rebuke you (B); punish you (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew does not name the object; Balanced and Readable make clear that God's rebuke would fall on the men if they came as traitors.

decisions.choice: as friends
decisions.reason: Readable puts "in peace" as coming with friendly intent.

records.source: וְר֣וּחַ לָבְשָׁ֗ה אֶת־עֲמָשַׂי֮ רֹ֣אשׁ הַשָּׁלִישִׁים֒ לְךָ֤ דָוִיד֙ וְעִמְּךָ֣ בֶן־יִשַׁ֔י שָׁל֨וֹם׀שָׁל֜וֹם לְךָ֗ וְשָׁלוֹם֙ לְעֹ֣זְרֶ֔ךָ כִּ֥י עֲזָרְךָ֖ אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ וַיְקַבְּלֵ֣ם דָּוִ֔יד וַֽיִּתְּנֵ֖ם בְּרָאשֵׁ֥י הַגְּדֽוּד׃פ
records.gloss: And [the] Spirit clothed Amasai, chief of the Thirty: To you, David, and with you, son of Jesse! Peace, peace to you, and peace to [the one] helping you, for has helped you your God. And received them David and set them among [the] heads of the band.
pieces: Then the Spirit clothed Amasai, chief of the Thirty, and he said, \q "We are yours, David! We are with you, son of Jesse! \q Peace, peace to you, and peace to whoever helps you, \q for your God helps you." \q So David welcomed them and made them leaders of his band.

L.19: And [the] Spirit clothed Amasai, chief of the Thirty: \q "[We are] yours, David, and with you, son of Jesse! \q Peace, peace to you, and peace to your helper, \q for your God helps you." \q And David received them and set them among the heads of the band.

R.19: Then the Spirit came on Amasai, the leader of the Thirty, and took hold of him. He said, \q "David, we are yours! Son of Jesse, we are on your side! \q May all go well with you, and with those who help you, \q because your God helps you." \q So David welcomed them and made them officers over his fighting men.

decisions.choice: the Spirit clothed Amasai: took hold of him completely
decisions.reason: The verb means to put on clothes. The Spirit wraps Amasai like a garment and speaks through him, as with Gideon (Judges 6:34) and the priest Zechariah (2 Chronicles 24:20). The Hebrew says only "spirit", but these parallels show it is the Spirit of God.

decisions.choice: chief of the Thirty: the reading of the traditional vowels
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew text has a word that means "officers" (chief of the officers); the traditional reading, followed here, gives "the Thirty", David's company of warriors, as in verse 4. Amasai is not named in the lists of 11:10-47; he may be the Amasa of 2:17 and 2 Samuel 17:25, but the text does not say.

decisions.choice: a short poem of loyalty: we belong to David because God is with him
decisions.reason: Amasai answers David's question of verse 18 in two pairs of lines. The men pledge themselves to David, wish him peace, and give the reason: God helps him. The word "help" runs through the chapter (verses 1, 18, 22, 23), and here God himself is David's helper.

decisions.choice: your helper: anyone who helps David
decisions.reason: The word is singular in form but stands for everyone who sides with David, including the men now speaking.

decisions.choice: the band: David's company of fighting men
decisions.reason: The word means a troop or raiding band. Here it is David's own band of followers (1 Samuel 22:2; 30:8).

decisions.choice: and he said; We are yours
decisions.reason: Hebrew moves straight from Amasai to his words and leaves out "we are"; Balanced and Readable supply both. The poem is set in lines.

decisions.choice: May all go well with you, and with those who help you
decisions.reason: "Peace" here is a wish for safety and well-being; Readable says so in plain words and does not repeat the word.

records.gloss: And from Manasseh fell to David when he came with [the] Philistines against Saul for the battle; and not they helped them, for by counsel sent him away [the] rulers of [the] Philistines, saying, At our heads he will fall to his lord Saul.
pieces: Some men of Manasseh also went over to David when he came with the Philistines to fight against Saul. But David and his men did not help the Philistines, because the rulers of the Philistines talked it over and sent him away. "He will go back to his master Saul," they said, "and it will cost us our heads."

L.20: And [some] from Manasseh fell to David when he came with the Philistines against Saul to battle; but they did not help them, for after counsel the rulers of the Philistines sent him away, saying, "At [the cost of] our heads he will fall to his lord Saul."

R.20: Some men from Manasseh left Saul and joined David when David went with the Philistines to fight against Saul. But in the end David's men did not help the Philistines. The Philistine rulers talked it over and sent David away. They said, "He will turn back to his master Saul, and we will lose our heads!"

decisions.choice: when he came with the Philistines against Saul: the battle at Gilboa
decisions.reason: David marched out with Achish king of Gath to the battle in which Saul died, but the Philistine leaders did not trust him and sent him back to Ziklag before it began (1 Samuel 29:1-11; 31:1-6).

decisions.choice: fell to David: deserted to him
decisions.reason: To "fall to" someone is to go over to his side (2 Kings 25:11). The same verb returns in the Philistines' words: David would "fall to" Saul, that is, go back to him.

decisions.choice: at our heads: at the cost of our lives
decisions.reason: The rulers fear that David would win back Saul's favor by turning on them in the battle. In 1 Samuel 29:4 they say he would do it "with the heads of these men"; here the heads at stake are their own.

decisions.choice: they did not help them: David and his men did not help the Philistines
decisions.reason: "They" are David and the men with him; "them" are the Philistines. The next clause gives the reason: the Philistines themselves sent David away.

decisions.choice: David and his men ... the Philistines
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who did not help whom, to make the pronouns clear.

decisions.choice: went over to David (B); left Saul and joined David (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture "fell to"; Balanced and Readable say what it meant.

decisions.choice: as he went to Ziklag: on the way back from the Philistine camp
decisions.reason: Sent away by the Philistine rulers, David went back to Ziklag and found it raided and burned (1 Samuel 29:11-30:1).

decisions.choice: heads of the thousands: commanders of the tribe's military units
decisions.reason: A "thousand" was a unit of a tribe's fighting men, led by its own commander (Numbers 31:14; 1 Samuel 29:2).

decisions.choice: commanders of thousands
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the usual military title; Literal keeps "heads".

L.22: And they helped David against the band, for all of them [were] mighty men of valor, and they were commanders in the army.

R.22: They helped David fight against the band of raiders, because they were all brave warriors. They became commanders in David's army.

decisions.choice: the band: the raiders who had burned Ziklag
decisions.reason: While David was away, Amalekite raiders burned Ziklag and took the families captive; David pursued this "band" and won everything back (1 Samuel 30:1-20, where the same word is used in 30:8, 15 and 23).

decisions.choice: mighty men of valor: as in verse 9
decisions.reason: As in verse 9.

decisions.choice: David's army
decisions.reason: Readable names whose army it was, which the context makes plain.

records.gloss: For at [the] time of day by day they came to David to help him, until [it was] a camp great like [the] camp of God.
pieces: Day after day men came to help David, until he had a great army, like the army of God.

L.23: For from day to day [men] came to David to help him, until [there was] a great camp, like the camp of God.

R.23: Every day more men came to help David, until his army was huge, as great as the army of God.

decisions.choice: like the camp of God: a vast army
decisions.reason: "Of God" can mark something as very great, as with "mountains of God" for mighty mountains (Psalm 36:7). It may also recall the camp of God's angels that Jacob saw (Genesis 32:3). Either way the army was immense.

decisions.choice: camp: an army in its camp
decisions.reason: The word means a camp and those camped in it, here David's growing army.

decisions.choice: army
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "camp"; Balanced and Readable say "army", which is what the camp was.

records.gloss: And these [are the] numbers of [the] heads of the armed for the army [who] came to David to Hebron to turn [the] kingdom of Saul to him according to [the] mouth of Yahweh.
pieces: These are the counts of the divisions armed for war that came to Hebron, to David, to turn the kingdom of Saul over to him, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said.

L.24: And these [are] the numbers of the heads of the armed [men] for the army [who] came to David at Hebron to turn the kingdom of Saul over to him, according to the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.24: Here are the numbers of the armed soldiers who came to David at Hebron. They came to give him Saul's kingdom, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had promised.

decisions.choice: came to David at Hebron: the gathering where David was made king over all Israel
decisions.reason: This is the assembly of 11:1-3 and 2 Samuel 5:1-3, where all Israel came to Hebron and anointed David king. Chapter 11 told it briefly; this list shows who came.

decisions.choice: to turn the kingdom of Saul over to him: as God had done
decisions.reason: The same words close the account of Saul's death: the LORD "turned the kingdom over to David" (10:14). What God decided, the tribes now carry out.

decisions.choice: according to the word of the LORD: as God had promised David
decisions.reason: God had chosen David and had Samuel anoint him (1 Samuel 16:1-13; compare 11:3, 10).

decisions.choice: the heads of the armed men: the companies or units of armed men
alternatives: the chiefs of the armed men
decisions.reason: "Heads" can mean leaders, but the numbers that follow count whole bodies of troops, not their chiefs; so here the word means the divisions or units that came.

decisions.choice: as the LORD had said (B); just as the LORD had promised (R)
decisions.reason: "The mouth of the LORD" means what the LORD said.

L.25: The sons of Judah bearing shield and spear: 6,800 armed for the army.

R.25: From Judah there were 6,800 soldiers armed for war, who carried shields and spears.

decisions.choice: six thousand eight hundred: on the size of these numbers
decisions.reason: As at Numbers 1:21, the word for "thousand" can also name a military unit (verse 21), which would make these totals smaller.

decisions.choice: shield and spear: the large shield and the heavy spear of foot soldiers
decisions.reason: The shield named here is the large body shield, and the spear the long thrusting spear, the arms of heavy infantry (compare 2 Chronicles 14:7).

decisions.choice: mighty men of valor: as in verse 9

decisions.choice: sons of Levi: the Levites, counted here with the fighting tribes
decisions.reason: The Levites were not counted among the tribes for war in Numbers (Numbers 1:47-49), but here they too come to Hebron to make David king, led by priests of Aaron's family (verses 28-29).

pieces: Jehoiada was leader of the house of Aaron, and 3,700 came with him.

L.28: And Jehoiada [was] the ruler for Aaron, and with him [were] 3,700.

R.28: Jehoiada was the leader of Aaron's family, and 3,700 men came with him.

decisions.choice: Jehoiada the leader for Aaron: head of the priestly family descended from Aaron
decisions.reason: Jehoiada led the priests. He may be the father of Benaiah, David's warrior, who is called the son of Jehoiada the priest in 27:5 (compare 11:22), but the text does not say so here.

decisions.choice: leader of the house of Aaron (B); leader of Aaron's family (R)
decisions.reason: The title usually given as "ruler" for a king or prince is kept at Literal. Here it names the head of a priestly family, so Balanced and Readable say "leader" and supply the family Aaron founded.

L.29: And Zadok, a young man, a mighty man of valor, and his father's house: twenty-two commanders.

R.29: Zadok, a brave young warrior, came too, with twenty-two leaders from his family.

decisions.choice: Zadok: later one of David's two chief priests
decisions.reason: Zadok became priest alongside Abiathar under David (2 Samuel 8:17; 1 Chronicles 18:16) and the high priest under Solomon (1 Kings 2:35). Here he is still a young man and is praised as a warrior.

decisions.choice: a mighty man of valor: as in verse 9
decisions.reason: As in verse 9, here of a single man.

records.gloss: And of [the] sons of Benjamin, kinsmen of Saul, three thousand; and until now their greater part [were] keeping [the] charge of [the] house of Saul.
pieces: From Benjamin, Saul's own kinsmen: 3,000. Until then most of them had stayed loyal to the house of Saul.

L.30: And of the sons of Benjamin, the kinsmen of Saul: 3,000; and until then the greater part of them [were] keeping the charge of the house of Saul.

R.30: From Benjamin, Saul's own tribe, there were 3,000. Until that time most of the people of Benjamin had stayed loyal to Saul's family.

decisions.choice: keeping the charge of the house of Saul: staying loyal to Saul's family
decisions.reason: To keep someone's charge is to stay at the post given by him. After Saul's death most of Benjamin had backed his son Ish-bosheth (2 Samuel 2:8-9; 3:19).

decisions.choice: until then: up to the time of this gathering
decisions.reason: The word means "until here" or "until now", seen from the time of the assembly at Hebron.

L.31: And of the sons of Ephraim: 20,800, mighty men of valor, men of names in the house of their fathers.

R.31: From Ephraim there were 20,800 brave warriors, each one famous in his family.

decisions.choice: men of names: famous men
decisions.reason: A man with a name is a man of renown (Genesis 6:4; Numbers 16:2).

decisions.choice: mighty men of valor: as in verse 9
decisions.reason: As in verse 9.

records.gloss: And of half of [the] tribe of Manasseh, eighteen thousand, who were designated by names to come to make king David.
pieces: From the half-tribe of Manasseh: 18,000, who had been named one by one to come and make David king.

L.32: And of the half-tribe of Manasseh: 18,000, who were designated by name to come to make David king.

R.32: From the half-tribe of Manasseh there were 18,000. They had been chosen by name to come and make David king.

decisions.choice: the half-tribe of Manasseh: the half west of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Manasseh lived in two halves, one on each side of the Jordan (Joshua 22:7). The eastern half is counted in verse 38, so this is the western half.

decisions.choice: designated by name: picked out and named for this purpose
decisions.reason: The verb is used of men named for a task (Numbers 1:17). Each man was chosen to go to Hebron.

records.gloss: And of [the] sons of Issachar, knowers of understanding for the times, to know what should do Israel; their heads two hundred, and all their kinsmen [were] at their mouth.
pieces: From Issachar: 200 chiefs, men with insight into the times, who knew what Israel ought to do, and all their kinsmen took orders from them.

L.33: And of the sons of Issachar, knowers of understanding of the times, to know what Israel should do: their heads [were] 200, and all their kinsmen [were] at their command.

R.33: From Issachar came 200 leaders. They had the wisdom to see what was happening in their day and to know what Israel should do. All their relatives followed their orders.

decisions.choice: who understood the times: men who saw what the moment called for
decisions.reason: "Knowing the times" means seeing what is happening and what should be done about it (Esther 1:13). These men saw that the time had come for Israel to make David king. Nothing in the words points to reading the stars.

decisions.choice: at their mouth: under their command
decisions.reason: "At the mouth of" someone means by his word or order (Genesis 41:40; Numbers 4:27).

decisions.choice: 200 chiefs: the number counts leaders only
decisions.reason: Unlike the other tribes, Issachar gives the number of its leaders, and says only that their kinsmen came with them.

records.gloss: Of Zebulun, goers out of [the] army, arrangers of battle with all weapons of war, fifty thousand, and to help with not heart and heart.
pieces: From Zebulun: 50,000 men ready for service in the army, drawn up for battle with every kind of weapon, who came to help with hearts that were not divided.

L.34: Of Zebulun, those going out [to the] army, setting the battle in order with all the weapons of war: 50,000, and to help with not a heart and a heart.

R.34: From Zebulun there were 50,000 soldiers ready for battle, armed with every kind of weapon. They came to help David and were loyal to him with all their heart.

decisions.choice: with not a heart and a heart: with undivided loyalty
decisions.reason: A man of "a heart and a heart" is double-minded and says one thing while meaning another (Psalm 12:3). These men had no such divided heart; they were wholly for David.

decisions.choice: to help: to join in the ranks
decisions.reason: The verb is rare. It may mean "to help" or "to stand in line, keep rank", linked to the verb for setting a battle in order; either way the men came ready to serve David's cause (compare verse 39).

decisions.choice: help David
decisions.reason: Readable names David, whom they came to help.

records.source: וּמִנַּפְתָּלִ֖י שָׂרִ֣ים אָ֑לֶף וְעִמָּהֶם֙ בְּצִנָּ֣ה וַחֲנִ֔ית שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים וְשִׁבְעָ֖ה אָֽלֶף׃ס
records.gloss: And of Naphtali, commanders one thousand, and with them with shield and spear thirty and seven thousand.
pieces: From Naphtali: 1,000 commanders, and with them 37,000 men carrying shield and spear.

L.35: And of Naphtali: 1,000 commanders, and with them, with shield and spear, 37,000.

R.35: From Naphtali there were 1,000 commanders, with 37,000 soldiers who carried shields and spears.

decisions.choice: spear: here a different word from verse 25
decisions.reason: Verse 25 has the heavy thrusting spear; the word here is the common one for a spear. Both are given as "spear".

decisions.choice: men carrying (B); soldiers who carried (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "with shield and spear"; Balanced and Readable name the men who bore them.

records.source: וּמִן־הַדָּנִי֙ עֹרְכֵ֣י מִלְחָמָ֔ה עֶשְׂרִֽים־וּשְׁמוֹנָ֥ה אֶ֖לֶף וְשֵׁ֥שׁ מֵאֽוֹת׃ס
records.gloss: And of the Danites, arrangers of battle: twenty and eight thousand and six hundred.
pieces: From Dan: 28,600 men drawn up for battle.

L.36: And of the Danites, setting the battle in order: 28,600.

R.36: From Dan there were 28,600 men ready to fight.

decisions.choice: setting the battle in order: trained and ready to take their place in the battle line
decisions.reason: The phrase describes men who can form a battle line (verses 34, 37; 1 Samuel 17:8).

records.source: וּמֵאָשֵׁ֗ר יוֹצְאֵ֥י צָבָ֛א לַעֲרֹ֥ךְ מִלְחָמָ֖ה אַרְבָּעִ֥ים אָֽלֶף׃ס
records.gloss: And of Asher, goers out of [the] army to arrange battle: forty thousand.
pieces: From Asher: 40,000 men ready for service in the army, to be drawn up for battle.

L.37: And of Asher, those going out [to the] army to set the battle in order: 40,000.

R.37: From Asher there were 40,000 soldiers ready to fight.

decisions.choice: going out to the army: fit for military service
decisions.reason: The phrase is used for men able to serve in war, as in the census of Numbers 1:3. It is used of Zebulun in verse 34.

records.gloss: And from beyond the Jordan, of the Reubenite and the Gadite and half of [the] tribe of Manasseh, with all weapons of [the] army of battle: one hundred and twenty thousand.
pieces: From across the Jordan, from Reuben, Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh: 120,000 men with every kind of weapon for battle.

L.38: And from across the Jordan, of the Reubenites and the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh, with all the weapons of the army for battle: 120,000.

R.38: From the east side of the Jordan River came 120,000 men from the tribes of Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh. They carried every kind of weapon.

decisions.choice: across the Jordan: east of the river
decisions.reason: Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh had their land east of the Jordan (Numbers 32:33; Joshua 13:8). The phrase is said from the point of view of the land west of the river, where Hebron lies.

decisions.choice: the east side of the Jordan River
decisions.reason: Readable names the direction.

records.source: כָּל־אֵ֜לֶּה אַנְשֵׁ֣י מִלְחָמָה֮ עֹדְרֵ֣י מַעֲרָכָה֒ בְּלֵבָ֤ב שָׁלֵם֙ בָּ֣אוּ חֶבְר֔וֹנָה לְהַמְלִ֥יךְ אֶת־דָּוִ֖יד עַל־כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְ֠גַם כָּל־שֵׁרִ֧ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל לֵ֥ב אֶחָ֖ד לְהַמְלִ֥יךְ אֶת־דָּוִֽיד׃
records.gloss: All these men of war, helping [the] battle line with a heart complete, came to Hebron to make king David over all Israel; and also all [the] rest of Israel [was] one heart to make king David.
pieces: All these fighting men, drawn up in battle order, came to Hebron with an undivided heart to make David king over all Israel. All the rest of Israel too were of one mind to make David king.

L.39: All these men of war, drawn up in battle line, came to Hebron with a complete heart to make David king over all Israel; and also all the rest of Israel [was of] one heart to make David king.

R.39: All these soldiers came to Hebron ready for battle. They were fully committed to making David king over all Israel. All the rest of the people of Israel also agreed that David should be king.

decisions.choice: with a complete heart: wholehearted and undivided
decisions.reason: A "complete" heart is whole and undivided, loyal without holding back (1 Kings 8:61; 1 Chronicles 28:9; 29:9). It sums up the "not a heart and a heart" of verse 34.

decisions.choice: one heart: of one mind
decisions.reason: The whole people agreed. The phrase picks up David's words in verse 18, "my heart will be one with you".

decisions.choice: drawn up in battle line: ready and in order for war
decisions.reason: The verb is rare and is spelled like the verb "help" in verse 34. It is usually taken as a form of the verb for setting troops in battle order, which suits the noun "battle line" beside it.

decisions.choice: fully committed; agreed
decisions.reason: Readable explains both heart pictures in plain words.

records.source: וַיִּהְיוּ־שָׁ֤ם עִם־דָּוִיד֙ יָמִ֣ים שְׁלוֹשָׁ֔ה אֹכְלִ֖ים וְשׁוֹתִ֑ים כִּֽי־הֵכִ֥ינוּ לָהֶ֖ם אֲחֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And they were there with David three days, eating and drinking, for had prepared for them their kinsmen.
pieces: They stayed there with David for three days, eating and drinking, because their kinsmen had provided for them.

L.40: And they were there with David three days, eating and drinking, for their kinsmen had prepared for them.

R.40: They stayed with David for three days, eating and drinking. Their relatives had prepared food for them.

decisions.choice: eating and drinking: a feast to celebrate the new king
decisions.reason: Making a king was marked with a feast (compare 1 Kings 1:25; 1 Chronicles 29:22). The assembly at Hebron ends in celebration.

decisions.choice: prepared food
decisions.reason: Readable names what the kinsmen prepared.

records.source: וְגַ֣ם הַקְּרֽוֹבִים־אֲ֠לֵיהֶם עַד־יִשָׂשכָ֨ר וּזְבֻל֜וּן וְנַפְתָּלִ֗י מְבִיאִ֣ים לֶ֡חֶם בַּחֲמוֹרִ֣ים וּבַגְּמַלִּ֣ים וּבַפְּרָדִ֣ים׀וּֽבַבָּקָ֡ר מַאֲכָ֡ל קֶ֠מַח דְּבֵלִ֨ים וְצִמּוּקִ֧ים וְיַֽיִן־וְשֶׁ֛מֶן וּבָקָ֥ר וְצֹ֖אן לָרֹ֑ב כִּ֥י שִׂמְחָ֖ה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ
records.gloss: And also those near to them, as far as Issachar and Zebulun and Naphtali, [were] bringing food on donkeys and on camels and on mules and on cattle, provisions of flour, fig cakes and raisin clusters and wine and oil and cattle and sheep in abundance; for joy [was] in Israel.
pieces: Their neighbors too, from as far away as Issachar, Zebulun and Naphtali, brought food on donkeys, camels, mules and oxen: plenty of flour, fig cakes, raisin cakes, wine, oil, cattle and sheep. For there was joy in Israel.

L.41: And also those near to them, as far as Issachar and Zebulun and Naphtali, were bringing food on donkeys and on camels and on mules and on oxen: provisions of flour, fig cakes and raisin cakes and wine and oil and cattle and sheep in abundance; for [there was] joy in Israel.

R.41: Their neighbors also brought food, even people from as far away as Issachar, Zebulun and Naphtali. They loaded it on donkeys, camels, mules and oxen. There was plenty of flour, fig cakes, raisins, wine, olive oil, cattle and sheep. Everyone in Israel was full of joy.

decisions.choice: those near to them, as far as Issachar, Zebulun and Naphtali: neighbors near and far
decisions.reason: Those near Hebron brought food, and so did tribes from far in the north. The whole land joined in.

decisions.choice: fig cakes and raisin cakes: pressed dried fruit that keeps and travels well
decisions.reason: Abigail brought the same kinds of food to David's men (1 Samuel 25:18).

decisions.choice: for there was joy in Israel: the people rejoiced in their king
decisions.reason: The chapter that began with a few men coming to David in hiding ends with all Israel rejoicing. Joy marks the great gatherings of worship and kingship in Chronicles (1 Chronicles 29:9, 22; 2 Chronicles 30:26).

decisions.choice: oxen (as carriers); cattle (as food)
decisions.reason: The same Hebrew word appears twice: first for animals that carried loads, then for animals brought to be eaten. Balanced and Readable use "oxen" for the first and "cattle" for the second.

decisions.choice: Everyone in Israel was full of joy
decisions.reason: Readable states the joy as something the people felt.
